text: Debugging is a normal part of programming. When your code does not work as expected, the first step is identifying bugs. You need to find out where the problem is and what causes it. Fortunately, many debugging tools can help you. For example, an IDE usually has a built-in debugger that lets you pause your program and check the values of variables. Another useful technique is logging. By adding print statements or log messages, you can see what your code is doing step by step. Most importantly, you should follow a systematic approach: test one change at a time, and avoid guessing.
